Step 2 of 4
Invite your team
Persona sets where each person lands and which studios and actions they see. An admin can fine-tune this per person or for every persona at once, later, in Users & Roles > Entitlements.
Persona is optional here. Anyone left as "Not set" gets least-privilege access until you assign a persona — they can suggest one at first sign-in, but it stays pending until you approve it in Users & Roles. Only you, as platform admin, is fixed, since that persona was chosen for you in step 1.

Framing

Problem statement
The bank now has several structured churn datasets, each with around 5,000 customer records and 38 behavioral and profile fields, but these tables are not yet being used to systematically identify customers at risk of closing accounts or sharply reducing usage. Today, retention and relationship teams still rely on generic rules and after-the-fact signals, even though the available data captures rich indicators such as tenure, balances, transaction patterns, digital channel usage, service interactions, complaints, loan and investment holdings, and an explicit churn outcome label.
Business description
Retail banking customers with records in the customer_churn_banking_5_k and related tables are affected because their experience is not yet guided by a data-driven view of their likelihood to leave or reduce engagement. Relationship managers, branch staff, and centralized retention teams cannot easily see which specific customers are flagged as high churn risk, nor prioritize by value using attributes such as Balance, TotalSpent, EstimatedSalary, AnnualIncome, InvestmentProducts, and InsuranceProducts.
AIFraming Agentsuggested framing · grounded on customer_churn_train_23, test_data, customer_churn_banking_5_k_fs_v3
Two additional churn tables should be profiled for schema alignment and label consistency before combining with the training set. No quantitative data-quality metrics are yet documented for individual fields.
Objectives
Use the structured churn tables to assign a churn-risk score to each active customer, enabling proactive retention actions before account closure.
Prioritize retention and relationship management efforts toward customers who are both high risk and high value.
Reduce overall churn and protect recurring revenue by integrating churn-risk scores into campaign selection and service workflows.
Create consistent, data-driven segments (low, medium, high churn risk) to support tailored offers and experience improvements.
KPIs
KPIBaselineTarget
Model discrimination performance on churn prediction (AUC on held-out test data)No validated AUC; current approach uses rules of thumbAchieve an AUC that clearly exceeds random classification, stable across segments

What this notebook does

Builds a store–campaign performance mart from skewed sales data, scoring stores and campaigns by revenue, discounts, and reach, then writes a final analysis table for downstream reporting or testing runtime plans.
Reads from
oneplatform_profit_pulse.default.sales_skewed
oneplatform_profit_pulse.default.stores
oneplatform_profit_pulse.default.items
oneplatform_profit_pulse.default.campaigns
Writes to
oneplatform_profit_pulse.default.final_store_campaign_industry_unoptimized_small
Languages
PYTHON
Key steps
  1. Read sales, stores, items, and campaigns tables (with row limits) and add bucketed/uppercased helper columns plus explicit repartition/sortWithinPartitions.
  2. Join orders to items, stores, and campaigns to create an enriched orders_campaign fact with revenue, discount_gap, and margin_band, then deduplicate and repartition.
  3. Aggregate orders_campaign to store-level metrics and compute a store_score based on sales, units, variety, and discount_gap.
  4. Aggregate orders_campaign to campaign-level metrics and compute campaign_efficiency, and separately build channel_margin_summary by channel/item_category/margin_band/store_type.
  5. Join store, campaign, and channel summaries into final_store_campaign_analysis, compute combined_performance_score, filter low-sales stores, repartition, and order by performance.
  6. Compute ranked_orders using a window over store_id and sales_channel, then log and write final_store_campaign_analysis as a Delta table with PlanLogger instrumentation.
Risk areas
  • Multiple explicit repartition() and sortWithinPartitions() calls may cause unnecessary shuffles and increase runtime if limits are removed or data grows.
  • Joins across four prepared datasets (orders, items, stores, campaigns) can become broad and expensive on large tables, especially with skewed keys.
  • Global orderBy() on final_store_campaign_analysis before write can be costly and is often unnecessary for Delta tables.
  • display() calls and full count() actions on large datasets will be slow and should be removed or guarded in production.
  • Hard-coded partition counts (e.g., 30, 35, 40, 50) may not scale well across environments with different cluster sizes.
